menu.title: Tidewater Market
menu.tagline: Grow a harbour town, one road and one trade at a time.

options.title: Options
options.videoNote: Video settings apply when the game runs in its own window.
options.pressKey: {action}: press a key or button (Esc cancels)
options.accessNote: Safe signals add patterns and marks. Reduced motion: no camera easing, no fading notices, a still title picture. Hold-free: clicks, not holds and drags. Each change applies at once and is saved.
options.conflict: {button} already does '{other}'. Pick another button for '{action}', or change '{other}' first.

road.name: Road
road.desc: Drag to lay a road. Warehouses and markets need one in front of their door.

house.name: House
house.desc: Four villagers live here. Needs a road next to it.

fisher_dock.name: Fisher dock
fisher_dock.desc: Catches fish. Must touch the water.

lumber_camp.name: Lumber camp
lumber_camp.desc: Cuts wood. Stands in a forest or on grass.

bakery.name: Bakery
bakery.desc: Bakes bread from flour, or from grain when there is no flour.

smokehouse.name: Smokehouse
smokehouse.desc: Smokes fish so it keeps and sells for more.

workshop.name: Workshop
workshop.desc: Makes tools from planks and stone.

warehouse.name: Warehouse
warehouse.desc: Stores goods; its workers carry goods between buildings.

market.name: Market
market.desc: Sells food to the villagers: keep it stocked and staffed.

pier.name: Pier
pier.desc: A landing for trading ships. Must touch the water; a ship needs open sea to reach it.

hud.speedHint: Speed: space pauses, 1 pause, 2 normal, 3 fast, 4 fastest

status.idle: B builds. Click a building or villager to look at it. Right-drag pans, the wheel zooms. F1 for help.
status.placing: {name}: {cost}.  Click to build, R to turn, Q or right-click to stop.
status.placingRoad: Road: drag to lay it, {cost} per piece.  Q or right-click to stop.
status.demolish: Demolish: click or drag over buildings. Half the cost comes back.  Q or right-click to stop.
status.paused: Paused. Press Space or 2 to go on.

reason.no_road: Needs a road in front of its door.

toast.broke: The town cannot pay all wages and upkeep today.

first_harbour.name: First Harbour
first_harbour.blurb: A quiet bay and an empty shore. Grow a small fishing town.

river_mills.name: River Mills
river_mills.blurb: A river valley with timber and stone. Feed a growing town with bread.

winter_trade.name: Winter Trade
winter_trade.blurb: The year turns to autumn. Smoke fish and bake bread before the cold.

sandbox.name: Sandbox
sandbox.blurb: Plenty of money and goods, and no goals. Build as you like.

won.title: {scenario} complete!
won.body: Every goal was reached by {date}. You can keep building, or go back to the title.

storm.title: Storm warning
storm.body: Black clouds pile up over the bay. The fishers drag their boats ashore and the wind already tugs at the [icon:wood] stacked on the quay.

result.secure: The crew lashes the stacks with [b]planks[/b] and rope. The storm howls over the town and takes [c:good]nothing[/c].

ride.0: Luck holds: the storm turns north and [c:good]spares the harbour[/c]. Nobody even loses a hat.
ride.1: The storm tears through the stacks and the nets. The town loses [c:bad]fish[/c] and [c:bad]wood[/c], and people grumble.

result.shelter: Everyone stays indoors. [c:muted]No harm done, but the sea stays empty for a while: the next ship is late.[/c]

festival.title: Midsummer festival
festival.body: The villagers want to celebrate the long days. Lanterns, music and [icon:bread] on every table would make the town [c:gold]talk about you for a year[/c].

result.feast: A great feast! Children dance in the squares and travellers carry the story to other ports. [c:gold]The town is proud.[/c]
result.stalls: A modest festival with a few stalls. It is pleasant and nobody complains.
result.skip: Work goes on as usual. [c:muted]Nobody mentions the festival, at least not to you.[/c]

merchant.title: A merchant's offer
merchant.body: A travelling merchant stops at the pier and opens his chest. He needs [icon:stone] and sells [icon:wood] cheap: [b]a fair deal[/b], if you want one.

result.buy_wood: The timber is cut and dry. A good price, and your stacks fill up.
result.sell_stone: He counts the coins slowly and loads the [icon:stone] onto his cart.
result.decline: He shrugs, tips his hat and goes on his way.

sick_herd.title: Sick herd
sick_herd.body: Several animals on the farms cough and refuse to graze. [c:bad]If it spreads, the grain stores will pay for it.[/c]

result.healer: The healer's herbs work. The herd is back on its feet within days, and the farmers remember who paid.
result.cull: A hard decision, but the meat sells and the rest of the herd is safe. Some villagers look away.

hope.1: It spreads. The farmers lose [c:bad]grain[/c] and pay for some emergency help.

good_harvest.title: A good harvest
good_harvest.body: The fields are heavier than anyone remembers. Sacks of [icon:grain] pile up at the farm gates: [c:good]more than the barns need[/c].

result.store: Carriers haul the extra grain to the warehouses until they groan.
result.sell: A trader from the south buys the surplus at a fine price.

fish_run.title: A run of fish
fish_run.body: The water boils with silver. A shoal of [icon:fish] is passing the bay, [b]once a year[/b], and the fishers ask for new nets.

choice.leave: Let them use the old ones

result.nets: The new nets come up heavy. The smokehouses will be busy.
result.leave: The old nets still catch something. The shoal passes.

cold_snap.title: Cold snap
cold_snap.body: Frost on the roofs, ice in the wells. The villagers shiver and look at the [icon:wood] you keep in the warehouses.

result.burn: Fires burn in every hearth. The villagers are warm and grateful, and the [c:bad]wood[/c] is gone.
result.blankets: Wool from the pedlars keeps the town warm. It costs [icon:coin] but not a log.
result.endure: The villagers endure, but they will remember it. [c:bad]The mood is sour.[/c]

wreck.title: A wreck on the rocks
wreck.body: A trading vessel broke up on the rocks at dawn. Planks and barrels wash ashore, and the harbour master wants to know [b]who gets them[/b].

choice.report: Report it to the shipping office

result.salvage: The crews drag the timber ashore before the tide takes it. [c:gold]Finders keepers.[/c]
result.report: You hand over the find and write the report. The office pays a reward and your name travels with the ships.

fire.title: Sparks at the sawmill
fire.body: A spark from the saw catches the dry [icon:planks] pile. Smoke rises over the roofs. [c:bad]It can still be put out, if someone acts now.[/c]

result.bucket: The whole town forms a line and the fire is out before it spreads. It costs a few coins in new buckets.

watch.0: The workers beat the flames out by themselves. [c:good]Close call![/c]
watch.1: The fire eats a stack of [c:bad]planks[/c] and [c:bad]wood[/c] before it dies out.

pedlar.title: The pedlar's cart
pedlar.body: A pedlar who has heard good things about the harbour parks his cart at the market. He sells [icon:tools] and gossip.

result.tools: Good steel, well made. The workshops are jealous.
result.gossip: You trade stories at the pier. By evening, three ports know the name of the town.

smugglers.title: Quiet visitors
smugglers.body: Two men in dark coats wait at the end of the pier after dusk. They offer [icon:coin] for the use of an empty warehouse. [c:bad]Nobody asks what is in the crates.[/c]

take.0: The crates leave at dawn and the coins stay. Nobody ever asks again.
take.1: The harbour guards find the crates. You pay a fine and your name is not so good at the harbour any more.

result.refuse: They leave without a word. The harbour master hears of it and nods.

letter.title: A letter from the Guild
letter.body: A letter arrives with the morning tide, sealed in green wax: [b]the Guild of Sea Traders[/b] will send ships to any town that builds a pier. Do you want the whole coast to know?

result.aloud: Within a day half the coast has heard. People come to look at your muddy shore. [c:gold]Expectations are high.[/c]
result.quiet: You keep the letter in a drawer. A quiet buyer pays you a few coins for a little silence.

pier.title: The first pier
pier.body: The pier stands. The planks smell of tar and new wood. The villagers ask whether it should have a name painted on its post, or whether plain is enough.

result.paint: A bright blue post and a gold name. Captains notice the harbour from far away.
result.plain: A plain pier, plain planks. It does the job.

cargo.title: The first cargo
cargo.body: The first order is filled and the captain shakes your hand. The crew asks where the first round of ale is. [icon:coin]

result.toast: The whole quay drinks to the harbour. [c:gold]The captain tells his friends.[/c]
result.pocket: You keep the coins. The captain frowns, and a rumour goes round that your harbour is stingy.

map.title: A place on the map
map.body: A cartographer wants to put [b]your town[/b] on the new sea charts. She needs a flag for the harbour, or she can write that the harbour is famous for its feasts.

result.flag: The flag flies from the pier, and the chart shows your town in gold ink. [c:gold]The Guild takes notice.[/c]
result.feast: The cartographer laughs and writes it down. Soon every captain wants to taste the legend.

bend.title: The bend in the river
bend.body: The river bends here and the current is strong. Millers say a mill would work well at this bend, if someone surveyed the stones first.

result.survey: The surveyor finds the best place and marks it. No stone will be wasted.
result.build: You will find the best place by trying.

grindstone.title: The grindstone
grindstone.body: The first mill needs a proper grindstone. A mason from upriver offers [icon:stone] cut for the purpose, or a worn one he only wants to lend.

result.buy: A fine stone, round and flat. It will grind for years.
result.borrow: The mason hands over some rough stone. He will remember it.

oven.title: The first loaf
oven.body: The bakery's oven is hot and the first loaves of [icon:bread] come out golden. The villagers queue at the door, but a merchant wants to buy the whole batch.

result.share: Every house gets a loaf. The bakery smells of happiness.
result.sell: The merchant pays well and the villagers go home hungry.

south.title: A contract from the south
south.body: Ships from the south want flour and bread every season, on a [b]long contract[/b]. It pays well but ties your mills to their calendar.

result.contract: The ink dries. The south will pay on time, and your mills will not rest.
result.freedom: You keep your freedom and your good name. The mills work for whoever pays best.

ice.title: Early ice
ice.body: The first ice forms in the bay. Old sailors say the sea will close for weeks. A merchant offers to deliver [icon:wood] for the winter before it does.

result.stock: The wood arrives just in time. The woodsheds are full.
result.trust: You keep your coins and trust the warehouses.

frost.title: The bay freezes
frost.body: A thin sheet of ice covers the bay. The ships hesitate. [b]A crew with axes[/b] could open a lane for them.

choice.break_ice: Pay a crew to break the ice

result.break_ice: The crew opens a lane, and the ships sail in. [c:gold]The captains remember who kept the harbour open.[/c]
result.wait: You wait. The ships will come, but later.

bargain.title: A hard bargain
bargain.body: A captain offers a very high price for [icon:smoked_fish] and then wants a discount, claiming the winter is hard everywhere. The villagers are watching.

result.haggle: You win the argument and the coins. He does not smile when he leaves.
result.fair: You treat him fairly. [c:gold]Word of it travels well.[/c]

thaw.title: The thaw
thaw.body: The ice breaks with a sound like thunder. Spring is coming. The villagers are tired of winter and want to [b]celebrate[/b].

result.celebrate: The whole town celebrates. [c:gold]A good winter, in the end.[/c]
result.save: You keep the barrels closed and the coins safe.
